notes:
Account summary: Aurora WealthTech (large national wealth manager) engaged for a broker-facing AI assistant (chat + reranking) and internal compliance summarization. Primary ask: FINRA-approved inference for customer-facing guidance and trade summarization. Red flags: must meet FINRA surveillance/archival controls and be auditable by their third-party audit team.

Key quotes: "We can't launch unless the platform passes FINRA controls and an external audit signoff" — Head of Compliance (M. Greene).

Timeline (high level):
- 2024-08-12: Lead created after intro from channel partner. AE: Sofia Martinez. SE engaged.
- 2024-09-02: Discovery call — identified use cases and rough throughput (peak 350 qps embedding/rerank, 20 qps chat). Latency SLO: 150-250ms token growth. Cost sensitivity: medium (must fit procurement model).
- 2024-10-21: POC kickoff — small sandbox on Redwood Dedicated; tested Llama-2, quantized variants. Early perf: 2x improvement with batching but compliance gaps still open.
- 2025-04-28: Security deep-dive (ff-20250428-aurora-sales-demo). Provided security pack: SOC2, ISO summary, audit logs, KMS integration guide. Requested FINRA-specific controls documentation.
- 2025-06-11: Legal + Compliance call (ff-20250611-security-call). Aurora requested written evidence of long-term retention controls, immutable audit trails, and traceability to operator. They escalated to external auditors.
- 2025-08-05: Aurora returns with procurement constraints: vendor must be on a pre-approved vendor list or complete FINRA vendor audit. They opted to run parallel vendor evaluation.
- 2025-09-10: Verbal update: Aurora decided to pilot with bank-internal provider and VendorX because those vendors already have pre-approved FINRA evidence. No active champion remains to sponsor further engagement.

POC notes / technical requirements:
- Preferred model family: tuned open models (Llama-family), but willing to consider Redwood-verified variants.
- Routing requirements: prefer region pinned to US-East with strong residency controls; automatic fallback to smaller quantized variant acceptable if fallbacks preserve audit trails.
- Observability: token-level traces and per-route retention for 7 years (FINRA requirement).
- Integration: SSO (SAML), KMS integration for customer-managed keys; on-prem option preferred for archival.

Deal outcome / current state:
- Status: Closed-lost (decision made internally by Aurora). Primary reason: Compliance blocker — FINRA pre-approval not achieved in timeframe and procurement selected vendor with existing FINRA evidence. Secondary: internal audit cycle/budget timeline misalignment.
- Ask for winback: capture formal FINRA rejection memo, offer whitepaper + third-party assessor to bridge gap, propose short technical spike to demonstrate immutable audit and retention controls.
- Next: AE to file closed-lost record, schedule internal post-mortem (owner: Sofia). SE to produce a FINRA-focused controls summary and checklist for future outreach.

CRM shorthand: 
- "lost to vendor w/ pre-approval; compliance said no"
- POC showed perf ok, compliance = blocker
- No active champion — procurement frozen until next audit cycle (Q3 2026)
